introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 2 pages (page de garde et six questions sur une page), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food &Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points des sous-questions imprimés totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(d), 3(a), 3(d), 4(c) et 5(a), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (3+2, 2+3, 5+5, 4+4, 2+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés (cinq, quatre, sept, huit...). D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste (types de repas, plats camerounais, équipements, signes de vieillissement de l'oeuf...) ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse, le sujet ne le détaille pas. La répartition des 10 points de 2(b) (2 par groupe) et de 6(a) (2,5 par équipement) est aussi une hypothèse.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : la liste des groupes de légumes (le sujet n'en impose aucune), les changements de l'oeuf qui vieillit (le sujet demande sept, d'autres manuels en donnent d'autres) et la température usuelle d'un congélateur (environ -18 degrés C). Aucune teneur nutritive ni durée de conservation chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de protéine (environ 17 kJ, valeur du programme).

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « State five(5) reasons » (1a), « pastry making . » (1d), « first aid box . » (3a ii), « State five (5) qualities of a good waiter? » (4a), « importance of studying » au singulier après « five (5) » (3d ii, 5a ii), « vegetables salads » (2d ii), « left-over foods » (6b).

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) qualities of a good waiter?

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five qualities (1 mark each):

1. **Clean and neat in appearance,** with good personal hygiene and a clean uniform.
2. **Polite and courteous** to every customer, with a pleasant and welcoming manner.
3. **Good knowledge of the menu,** the dishes, the drinks and the way of service, so that he or she can advise customers.
4. **Quick, efficient and attentive,** serving customers promptly and noticing their needs.
5. **Honest and reliable,** handling food, money and bills with honesty, and patient even with a difficult customer.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline five (5) points to consider when choosing a refrigerator.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five points (1 mark each):

1. **Size (capacity)** - suitable for the size of the family and the space in the kitchen.
2. **Running cost** - it should use little electricity (an energy-saving model).
3. **Price and guarantee** - the cost must be within the family budget and the make should have a guarantee, available spare parts and after-sales service.
4. **Features** - a freezer compartment, adjustable shelves, a thermostat to control the temperature and a vegetable drawer.
5. **Ease of cleaning and durability** - a smooth, strong finish that is easy to clean inside and outside, with a well-fitting door.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Enumerate four (4) reasons for eating food.

(4 marks)

(ii) State four (4) functions of proteins in the body.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Four reasons for eating food (1 mark each).**

1. To **supply energy** for work, movement and keeping the body warm.
2. For **growth** of the body, especially in children.
3. For **repair of worn-out and damaged tissues.**
4. To **protect the body against diseases** and to regulate body processes (with vitamins, minerals and water).

(Satisfying hunger and giving enjoyment of meals would also be accepted.)

**(ii) Four functions of proteins in the body (1 mark each).**

1. They are needed for **growth** of new cells and tissues.
2. They **repair** worn-out and damaged cells and tissues.
3. They are used to make **enzymes, hormones and antibodies** (which fight infection).
4. They **supply energy** (about 17 kJ per gram) when carbohydrates and fats are not enough.
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline seven (7) changes that take place when an egg is getting older.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
As an egg gets older the following changes take place (1 mark each):

1. The **shell loses its protective coating (bloom),** so the pores are open and air and bacteria can pass in more easily.
2. **Water evaporates through the pores,** so the contents shrink and the **air space** at the broad end of the egg becomes **larger.**
3. The egg becomes **lighter:** in water a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, an older egg tilts or stands on end, and a very old egg floats.
4. The **white becomes thin and watery** and spreads out widely when the egg is broken (the thick white is lost).
5. The **yolk membrane weakens,** so the yolk becomes flat and breaks easily.
6. The **yolk is no longer held in the centre** (the chalazae weaken) and moves towards the shell.
7. When it is very old the egg **develops an unpleasant sulphur smell and taste** because bacteria have entered and decomposed the contents.
